title: LDAEP and resting-state EEG in healthy women
description: EEG recordings from 69 healthy women (aged 19-40) collected at the Department of Psychology, University of Oslo, to study the relationship between hormonal contraceptive use and central serotonergic activity indexed by the loudness dependence of auditory evoked potentials (LDAEP). Each participant completed eyes-closed and eyes-open resting-state recordings, and 54 also completed an LDAEP auditory paradigm. Phenotype data cover hormonal contraceptive use, menstrual cycle phase, depressive symptoms (BDI-II), impulsivity (UPPS-P), and lifestyle factors.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a BioSemi ActiveTwo system using 64 Ag-AgCl electrodes placed according to the extended 10-20 system, plus 4 EOG channels, at a 2048 Hz sampling rate. The resting-state recording (4 minutes eyes closed, then 4 minutes eyes open) was always done first. The LDAEP paradigm used 1000 Hz tones at five intensities (55, 65, 75, 85 and 95 dB SPL), with 80 trials per level. Raw data are stored in BrainVision format and were organised into BIDS with MNE-BIDS.
